sources.title: Azuonye 1992 official landing page and local PDF
sources.status: verified landing page; local PDF archived
sources.evidence: Azuonye frames the work as a study of origins, features, significance, mechanics, possibilities, and problems of the Nwagu Aneke Igbo Syllabary.
sources.label: EXTERNAL+OBSERVED

sources.title: Azuonye Appendix I chart render
sources.evidence: The rendered chart shows 26 printed consonant rows and 8 vowel columns; f/v is a combined row.
sources.label: OBSERVED

sources.title: Omniglot Nwagu Aneke page
sources.status: web page and local HTML archived
sources.evidence: Describes the script as a syllabary for Umuleri Igbo, left-to-right, with logographic symbols and no independent vowels.
sources.label: EXTERNAL

sources.title: Ahamefula 2012 USEM article
sources.status: web text located; not locally archived by this script
sources.evidence: Reports 224 ideal Igbo syllabary symbols, 164 actual Aneke symbols, around 30 multivalent characters, ten duplicate-symbol syllables, and f/v sharing.
sources.label: EXTERNAL

sources.title: Unicode L2/23-203 African scripts update
sources.evidence: Lists Nwagu Aneke as an unencoded syllabary with some logographic symbols, written left to right, and notes more than 100 books.
sources.label: EXTERNAL

sources.title: Oxford Handbook of African Languages chapter
sources.evidence: Places the Nwagu Aneke Igbo syllabary among recent African orthography and writing-system inventions.
sources.label: EXTERNAL

claims.claim: The research object is not a modifier atlas; it is the Nwagu Aneke script and archive.
claims.evidence: Repo AGENTS.md and research/pagc/WIKI.md identify PAGC as a program around Nwagu Aneke source-derived structure.

claims.claim: The 27-base figure is not source-observed in the chart; it is derived only if f/v is split.
claims.evidence: EXP-0001 and corpus inventory observations INV-0001 through INV-0004.

claims.claim: Ahamefula adds a richer count problem: 224 ideal syllables vs 164 actual symbols.
claims.evidence: USEM article lines 1134-1138; needs local archival and line-verified extraction before becoming a repo claim.

claims.claim: The f/v collapse is not a nuisance; it is a linguistic feature of the Umuleri-specific repertoire.
claims.evidence: USEM article lines 1148-1152 plus EXP-0001 f/v row audit.

claims.claim: Logographs must be modeled as a separate inventory from CV syllabary cells.
claims.evidence: Omniglot feature list, Azuonye appendix audit, and Ahamefula logograph examples.

claims.claim: A Unicode/repertoire proposal would require a character inventory, names, glyph sources, usage evidence, and community review.
claims.evidence: Unicode status document says no encoding proposal yet; additional proposal requirements are inferred from standards practice, not proven here.

threads.title: Repertoire Reconstruction

threads.title: Ideal vs Actual Syllabary Space
threads.question: Why does Ahamefula say Igbo would require 224 symbols, while the Aneke syllabary has 164?
